title: Offshore counter-drone: the money is funded for ports and airfields, the demonstrated need is a platform 80 nautical miles offshore
map_limitation: Six blind spots specific to THIS map. (1) The money and the need are in different documents and no fetched source closes the gap. The NATO announcement carrying the more than $40 billion names the nodes it protects as ports, railheads, airfields, ammunition depots and forward assembly areas, and the maritime hook is a scope sentence in a European Parliamentary Research Service note listing maritime security systems inside Eastern Flank Watch, which is a scope statement and not an earmark. Nothing fetched in this run prices counter-drone protection of fixed offshore energy installations as its own pool, so every money figure on this map belongs to the enclosing programme and none of it is attributed to this application. That is the load-bearing weakness, and it is the thesis the map was built to test rather than a defect discovered afterwards. (2) The links closest to the occurrence are the least listed, and the census is deliberately not clean. The named counter-drone weapon station, its electro-optics and its integrator are one Israeli state-owned group and its subsidiary (Rafael, Controp); the drone-detection radar, fusion software, intruder sonar and thermal wide-area vendors that fetched sources name are private (Robin Radar, Cambridge Pixel, Sonardyne, HGH Infrared, D-Fend Solutions, Terma, which is Danish foundation-owned); the largest named political violence lead is a private Lloyd's managing agency (Aegis London); and the naval response is three sovereign navies. uncrewed-patrol-and-mcm-response therefore carries zero tickers, counter-uas-funding-and-requirements carries zero by design, and short-range-effectors carries two reached through a radar named inside somebody else's weapon station. Those are findings about the chain, not gaps in the search. (3) Supplier-side EDGAR full-text search cannot reach most of this map: fifteen of the nineteen distinct tickers here file outside the SEC (HAG.DE, KOG.OL, HO.PA, LDO.MI, DRO.AX, 218410.KQ, SPM.MI, CS.PA, OMV.VI, SNP.RO, SNG.RO, EQNR.OL, TTE.PA, MUV2.DE, SREN.SW), so they enter through research rather than through fts and their disclosure granularity is set by their own regulators, not by Regulation S-K. (4) Four cited pages carry no publication date and are dated to the day they were fetched, 2026-08-30: Cambridge Pixel, HENSOLDT, Sonardyne and AXA XL. Their content is current as read; their age is unknown. (5) The insurance half is directionally sourced. The only Black Sea premium print that opened is a percentage of a vessel's HULL value, which belongs to the moving-hull book on hormuz-maritime and not to this one, and no fetched source prices war or property cover on a fixed offshore installation anywhere. The repricing this map's underwriting link would carry is therefore a hypothesis with a wording citation behind it and no number. (6) Seven pages were fetched and refused and none of them contributed a link, an edge or a ticker: Terma's drone-detection page (403), globalsecurity.org and NATO Allied Maritime Command on Baltic Sentry (403 each), Qorvo's X-band radar note (429, twice), Military Embedded Systems on GaN in AESA radar (503, twice), Thales' own EagleShield page (empty body, so the Thales evidence comes from trade press instead), and Overt Defense on the Kongsberg award (402 paywall, so World Oil carries it instead).

scenarios.narrative: The gap this map was built to test closes on paper. After a hit, nobody buys a sensor; they buy a system that was supposed to have cued a response, which is this layer.
The cost exchange of answering a cheap craft with a fighter sortie becomes politically indefensible the moment one gets through.
A surface hit immediately raises the question of what is under the platform, which no radar answers.
The state response scales first because it is the only capability that already exists and can be ordered in days.

scenarios.title: The drone wall absorbs it and offshore stays a footnote
scenarios.narrative: The money does exactly what its own text says. Ports, railheads, airfields, ammunition depots and forward assembly areas get the sensors and the effectors, the marketplace fills with land and air systems, and the offshore case stays what it is today: a scope sentence, a handful of vendor pages and an operator paying for its own guards. The listed names on this map keep re-rating on the land programme, the maritime variant never becomes a product line, and anyone who bought this chain bought European defence beta with extra steps. This is the base case, it is why the only money corner on the map is a software layer rather than a box, and it is the case the map has to be able to lose to.

notes.text: THE THESIS WAS TESTED AND IT HOLDS, LITERALLY. The card says the money is announced in one domain and the demonstrated need is in another. That is now a cited fact rather than a reading: the NATO announcement that carries the more than $40 billion states that the alliance's ability to move forces across ports, railheads, airfields, ammunition depots and forward assembly areas depends on keeping those nodes usable, and the same page's detection and defeat inventories name radars, RF sensors, cameras, acoustic arrays, jammers, high-power microwave, interceptor drones, airburst cannon and nets without a single sea-based or offshore application. The only maritime hook that opened is the European Parliamentary Research Service note listing maritime security systems inside Eastern Flank Watch, which is scope and not money. So the gap the card asserts is real, and the map's honest position is that links 3 through 8 are being built against a requirement that does not yet name them.

THE UNLISTED SHARE, WHICH IS THE HANDOFF NELL ASKED FOR. The card said to expect a large unlisted share and to treat a clean pure-play census as evidence of a mapping error. The census came back exactly that way and is recorded rather than tidied: 2 of 13 links carry zero tickers, 3 carry one, and the two links nearest the occurrence, the effector and the naval response, are the thinnest on the map. The single cleanest listed pure play on the whole chain, DRO.AX at rf-detection-and-jamming, sits on the layer least likely to answer the actual threat, because an explosive one-way surface craft has no control link to jam. That inversion, the best listed access sitting on the least relevant defeat mechanism, is this map's sharpest single finding and it is the first thing the heat stage should attack.

SHARED LINK DECLARED FROM THIS SIDE. reinsurance-and-lloyds-capacity is the one link this chain shares with hormuz-maritime, matching the declaration already made from that side on its war-risk-reinsurance-capacity link. The shared thing is the Lloyd's syndicate and reinsurance capital layer and nothing below it. This chain's primary book, offshore-war-and-property-underwriting, is upstream energy property cover on FIXED installations with offshore war and terrorism perils extended onto it, attaching to an asset that cannot leave a listed area; hormuz-maritime's is war hull, war P&I and war cargo on MOVING hulls, cancellable at short notice and repriced per voyage. Different policy, different loss model, different renewal cycle. The three tickers on this chain's reinsurance link (MUV2.DE, SREN.SW, CB) are a deliberate subset of the eight on the hormuz link and are seeds inherited from the declaration, not names any source fetched for this chain places on this occurrence. A screen must count a position in any of them once across both maps.

ARCHETYPES. Applied: ARCH-003 (the uninvestable order-book owner) on counter-uas-funding-and-requirements, the fourth chain in a row whose root is a party that publishes a schedule and no equity, and here it carries an extra finding because the schedule names land and air nodes only. ARCH-006 (geopolitical counter-response as a first-class link) on uncrewed-patrol-and-mcm-response, its third chain, which takes the archetype past the one-instance Watch note it carried into this run. ARCH-002 (EPC volume without capture) on platform-integration-and-hardening, with the trap named in the bottleneck note rather than implied: scarce heavy-lift vessels inside a competitively bid contracting model, where the scarcity does not reach the margin. ARCH-001 (precision manufacturing capacity as the gating step) on rf-and-radar-front-end-components in its component form, where the cited constraint is GaN-on-SiC foundry access rather than amplifier design; scored HIGH rather than CHOKE_POINT because nothing fetched ties that constraint to this application. Checked and did NOT fire: ARCH-004 (critical material input), because no fetched source names a material at any stage of this chain, which is what separates a sensor chain from a munitions chain; ARCH-005 (power and grid equipment behind someone else's story), no grid layer exists on this map; ARCH-007 (semis as a leaf), the nearest analogue is rf-and-radar-front-end-components, and it is deliberately NOT scored as a leaf because the cited foundry constraint makes it a gating input rather than a famous ticker included for completeness. No archetype was overridden and none conflicted.

STAGES CHECKED AND NOT BUILT, each because nothing citable tied it to this occurrence or to this application. (1) Private offshore guard and security services, guard vessels and armed teams: the layer obviously exists and hormuz-maritime carries its moving-hull equivalent, but three searches returned only vendor pages about drone INSPECTION of platforms and offshore wind O&M contracts, and no fetched source put a named security provider on a fixed offshore energy asset. It stays out rather than being cited from a search snippet. (2) Maritime domain awareness data and analytics as its own link (AIS, satellite, behavioural analytics): every fetched source describes AIS as one feed inside a fusion product rather than as a separately bought stage, so it is folded into c2-and-sensor-fusion instead of given a link it did not earn. (3) Directed energy as its own link: high-power microwave appears once inside the alliance's non-kinetic inventory and lasers appear once as a dazzler in a deterrent list, and neither is enough for a stage, so both sit inside the effector and sensing links that cite them. (4) Interceptor drone manufacturing as a separate stage from effectors: named in the kinetic-defeat inventory, but no fetched source attaches a maker or a programme to a maritime or offshore use, so it is inside short-range-effectors. (5) Claims adjusting, salvage and wreck removal on a struck offshore installation: no cited source establishes any claims activity at all on this occurrence, which is itself the finding, because premium with no visible claims is the thing the heat stage most needs to test. (6) Crew willingness and offshore manning, which was the decisive correction on hormuz-maritime: nothing fetched for this occurrence says anything about whether platform crews will keep working, and the analogue is flagged here as a question for the heat stage rather than borrowed across chains.

THE COST EXCHANGE IS THE ECONOMIC QUESTION AND IT IS RECORDED, NOT SCORED. Three cited facts point the same way and belong to the heat stage rather than to this one. The buyer has published a ceiling: less than $150,000 per round in a quantity buy of at least 5,000, compatible with an existing launcher, which is a specification written to invite substitution. The cited fixed-installation weapon station is a 20-foot container-footprint module, which is a form factor designed to be commoditised and lifted by anybody's crane. And every sensor link on this map terminates in one fusion link whose own sources say data fusion rather than raw detection is becoming central. If capture exists on this chain it is at c2-and-sensor-fusion and at subsea-and-underwater-sensing, not at the effector, and the map records that as cited capture_inputs with the margin field NULL at every link, because no fetched source discloses margin anywhere on this chain.
